sentence: Vitamin D deficiency means the body does not have enough vitamin D.
note: MedlinePlus and NICE CKS pages are titled and framed on vitamin D deficiency; definition is a plain restatement.

sentence: The skin makes vitamin D from summer sunlight, and in the UK sunlight is not strong enough in the autumn and winter to make enough.
note: Returned NHS text: skin makes vitamin D from summer sunlight; UK sunlight too weak from autumn to spring.

sentence: Food supplies only a small share of the vitamin D most people need.
note: Returned text: food supplies only a small share (one NHS leaflet puts it at around a tenth); NHS Inform listed food sources.

sentence: Oily fish, egg yolks, red meat, and fortified cereals and spreads are the main food sources.
note: NHS Inform summary listed these sources.

sentence: Two common drivers of deficiency are a low intake of foods containing vitamin D and reduced time in the sun.
note: StatPearls summary: decreased intake of vitamin D containing food and reduced sun exposure.

sentence: Clinicians do not fully agree on the blood level that should count as deficient, and different guidelines give different definitions.
note: CKS: no clear consensus on the threshold for adults; review noted greatly varying definitions.

sentence: Many people with low vitamin D have no symptoms, or only vague ones.
note: NHS 111 Wales summary: most people have no symptoms, or only vague ones such as tiredness or aches.

sentence: For this reason the problem is often found only when a doctor has a reason to look for it.
note: CKS: testing is recommended mainly where symptoms may be due to low vitamin D or there is a clinical reason, such as a fall.

sentence: Vague symptoms such as tiredness and general aches are the most common picture.
note: NHS 111 Wales summary: vague symptoms include tiredness or aches.

sentence: In adults, prolonged or severe deficiency can cause bone pain, joint pain, muscle pain, fatigue, muscle twitching and weakness.
note: StatPearls summary: bone pain, arthralgia, myalgia, fatigue, fasciculations and weakness.

sentence: Because these symptoms are unspecific and very common, clinicians can over-suspect the condition.
note: StatPearls summary said symptoms are unspecific and common so deficiency may be over-suspected.

sentence: Osteomalacia, a softening of the bones in adults, is the adult bone disease most clearly linked to vitamin D deficiency, and it causes weak bones, bone pain and muscle weakness.
note: MedlinePlus overview: weak bones, bone pain, muscle weakness; Scottish study: osteomalacia is the only adult bone disease unequivocally linked to deficiency.

sentence: UK guidance lists muscle aches and weakness, especially in the thigh and buttock muscles, a waddling walk, and long-lasting widespread pain.
note: Returned UK guidance text listed muscle aches and weakness in quadriceps and glutei, waddling gait and chronic widespread pain.

sentence: In children, the equivalent bone condition is rickets, which can cause bowed legs, bone pain, muscle weakness and a waddling walk.
note: NHS 111 Wales: bowed legs main sign of rickets; bone pain, muscle weakness, waddling.

sentence: Children with deficiency may also be irritable or lethargic, have delayed development, bone changes or fractures.
Very rarely, low calcium linked to the problem can cause cramps and seizures.
note: NHS 111 Wales summary: very rarely low calcium causes cramps and seizures.

sentence: Deficiency tends to arise when too little vitamin D is taken in, too little is made by the skin, or the body cannot absorb or use it well.
note: StatPearls summary: reduced intake and sun exposure, malabsorption and drugs among causes.

sentence: Other factors named in medical reviews include darker skin, malabsorption syndromes, some medicines such as corticosteroids, ageing, smoking, obesity, and liver or kidney disease.
The NHS says people who rarely go outdoors, live in a care home or usually cover most of their skin outside are less likely to make enough vitamin D from sunlight.
note: NHS summary of groups advised to supplement year-round.

sentence: People with dark skin, such as those of African, African-Caribbean or South Asian background, may also make less vitamin D from sunlight.
NICE public health work on prevention also names infants and young children, pregnant and breastfeeding women, and people over 65.
note: NICE pathway text listed these groups to target for prevention.

sentence: The US National Institutes of Health notes that breastfed infants, people with conditions that limit fat absorption such as Crohn's disease, coeliac disease or ulcerative colitis, and people who have had certain operations are more likely to have trouble getting enough.
note: ODS consumer fact sheet text as returned (US spelling celiac).

sentence: Vitamin D status is measured with a blood test for 25-hydroxyvitamin D, the most stable form of the vitamin.
note: StatPearls: status determined by 25-hydroxyvitamin D serum concentration; UK guideline: routine labs measure the most stable form.

sentence: A GP may arrange a blood test for vitamin D and calcium if a person has symptoms or risk factors.
NICE CKS says testing everyone is not recommended; testing is advised when musculoskeletal symptoms may be due to low vitamin D or there is a clinical reason, such as a recent fall.
note: CKS summary: universal screening only recommended in those situations; NICE advises not to routinely test people without symptoms (summary text, page not individually attributed).

sentence: If osteomalacia is suspected, doctors may also check blood calcium, phosphate and alkaline phosphatase, sometimes parathyroid hormone, and may arrange an X-ray of the painful area.
note: Returned summary of an NHS Nottinghamshire guideline workup; page title is children's guidance, so attribution is cautious.

sentence: A low vitamin D result alone does not establish osteomalacia, which is defined by abnormal bone-related blood results.
note: Scottish study: biochemical osteomalacia defined by abnormal calcium, parathyroid hormone or alkaline phosphatase.

sentence: Treatment usually involves vitamin D supplements, together with attention to diet and sensible sun exposure.
note: NHS 111 Wales/NHS summary: treatment is usually supplements plus diet and sun exposure.

sentence: NICE CKS describes an initial period of higher-dose vitamin D followed by a lower daily maintenance supplement.
note: CKS summary: high-dose vitamin D for a number of weeks then daily maintenance (numbers deliberately omitted).

sentence: Follow-up is used to confirm that levels have corrected and to watch for toxicity, which usually shows as a high blood calcium.
note: CKS and StatPearls summaries: follow-up to check for toxicity, usually hypercalcaemia.

sentence: The NHS advises that everyone should consider a daily vitamin D supplement during the autumn and winter, and some groups are advised to take one all year.
Taking too much over a long time can raise calcium in the blood, which may weaken bones and damage the kidneys and heart.
Sunlight cannot cause vitamin D overdose, but skin still needs protection from sunburn and skin cancer.
A routine GP appointment is the usual route for persistent bone pain, muscle weakness or aches, or for a child with bowed legs.
note: Symptoms from returned text; routing is the site signposting rule.

sentence: A GP can arrange a blood test and decide whether treatment is needed.
note: NHS 111 Wales summary: GP may order blood test if symptoms or risk factors.

sentence: Persistent musculoskeletal pain can lead to referral or specialist advice when it does not have a clear cause.
note: Search summary: persistent musculoskeletal pain warrants referral or seeking specialist advice; page attribution uncertain.

sentence: Call NHS 111 or contact the GP the same day for muscle cramps or spasms that are new and unexplained.
note: Site signposting rule; route to care named, not from a source.

sentence: Call 999 for a seizure.
note: Site signposting rule; route to care named, not from a source.

sentence: People who think they are at higher risk can ask the GP or pharmacist whether a supplement is suitable for them.
note: Site signposting rule; route to care named, not from a source. NHS page names groups advised to supplement.

sentence: Supplements should not be taken in excess, because too much can raise blood calcium.
Clinicians also take care with supplementation to avoid adverse effects, which is one reason follow-up matters.
note: Summaries: follow-up to assess for toxicity; special attention to supplementation to prevent adverse effects.

sentence: Treatment usually aims to restore vitamin D with supplements, alongside diet and sun exposure.
Follow-up checks whether levels have corrected and whether any toxicity has developed.
Whether symptoms such as bone pain improve depends on the person and the cause, and a GP can advise.
note: General statement; no source claim made.

sentence: Tiredness is one of the vague symptoms the NHS lists, but many people with low vitamin D have no symptoms.
Because tiredness is very common and unspecific, it does not on its own show that vitamin D is low.
A GP can look for other causes.
In the summer months the skin can make vitamin D from sunlight.
In the autumn and winter, UK sunlight is not strong enough to make enough.
The NHS advises everyone to consider a daily supplement during those seasons, and some people are advised to take one all year.
Skin still needs protection from sunburn.
Yes, over a long period too much can raise calcium in the blood, which may weaken bones and damage the kidneys and heart.
Sunlight does not cause overdose.
The NHS gives upper limits for supplements, so a pharmacist or GP can advise on suitable products.
note: NHS says it gives limits for adults and lower limits for children.

sentence: NICE CKS says testing everyone is not recommended.
It advises testing when muscle or bone symptoms may be due to low vitamin D, or when there is another clinical reason such as a recent fall.
The decision is made by the clinician.
Rickets is the childhood form of bone softening linked to low vitamin D, and osteomalacia is the adult form.
note: NHS 111 Wales page title and summary.

sentence: Rickets can cause bowed legs, while osteomalacia brings bone pain and muscle weakness.
A GP can arrange tests if either is suspected.
note: NHS 111 Wales: GP may order blood tests.

sentence: Also called: Low vitamin D; hypovitaminosis D; with bone effects, rickets (children) and osteomalacia (adults)
note: Terms from NHS 111 Wales and MedlinePlus.

sentence: Main sources of vitamin D: Sunlight on the skin in summer, plus a smaller share from food and supplements
Often found: Many people have no symptoms or only vague ones, such as tiredness or aches
Usually diagnosed by: A blood test for 25-hydroxyvitamin D, when symptoms or risk factors suggest it
Usual treatment: Vitamin D supplements with diet and sun exposure, then follow-up
Groups at higher risk: Little time outdoors, covered skin, dark skin, care-home residents, older people, some gut conditions
A shortage of vitamin D in the body, which can weaken bones and muscles over time.

sentence: Vitamin D deficiency means the body does not have enough vitamin D. The skin makes it from summer sunlight, and food supplies only a small share, so in the UK autumn and winter sunlight is too weak to meet needs. Many people have no symptoms or only vague ones such as tiredness and aches. Prolonged or severe deficiency can affect the bones and muscles, causing rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
note: Combines sentences from the article section ledger: NHS 111 Wales, NHS Inform, StatPearls, MedlinePlus.

Diagnosis is usually by a blood test for 25-hydroxyvitamin D, requested when symptoms or risk factors suggest it. Experts do not fully agree on the level that counts as deficient, and routine testing of people without symptoms is not recommended. If osteomalacia is suspected, bone-related blood tests and sometimes an X-ray are used.

Contact a GP for a routine appointment about persistent bone pain, muscle weakness or aches, or a child with bowed legs. Contact NHS 111 or the GP the same day for new unexplained muscle cramps. Call 999 for a seizure.
